thread:
maya: quick update 1: we spun a small shadow of rerank-q3-int4 against the long-doc evaluation group overnight. Latency down ~22%, cost ~-30%, but MRR on long-doc slice dipped ~1.8%.
sam: numbers? sample size?
maya: ~4.8k shadowed requests over 5.5h, focused on docs >3k tokens. baseline MRR=0.4119, rerank-q3 MRR=0.4039, p~0.018. product-global MRR flat.
jordan: ugh that p is borderline. our old auto-fallback is a blunt instrument for long-doc. we should make slice-aware gates.
evan: current canary auto-fallback rule: any key-metric relative drop >2% AND p<0.01 OR absolute drop >0.03 triggers fallback. tuned for shortform/topline signals.
maya: long-doc variance is higher; this rule would flip us too often. propose relaxing p cutoff but adding effect-size and distribution-shift checks.
sam: suggest combined criteria: require relative drop >1.5% AND Cohen's d >0.18 OR sustained decline across 3 rolling windows. plus entropy shift guard.
jordan: agree on entropy. rerank-q3 tightened score distribution (avg pairwise entropy -8%). lower entropy might reduce exploration in long contexts. tie that to rollback.
evan: we already compute per-session pairwise score entropy in telemetry. can hook that into canary engine.
sam: draft canary config:
```
canary:
  duration: 48h
  global_sample: 5%
  slices:
    - id: long-doc
      matcher: "tokens > 3000"
      initial_traffic: 0%
      ramp_policy: "manual-tilt"
  autosafety:
    quality_metric: long_doc_MRR
    relative_threshold: 0.015
    absolute_threshold: 0.02
    pvalue_cutoff: 0.01
    cohen_d_min: 0.18
    sustain_windows: 3
    entropy_guard:
      enabled: true
      relative_entropy_drop: 0.10
      require_mrr_drop: 0.01
```
Start with 0% for long-doc, run shadow A/B for 48h at 10% targeted routing baseline vs rerank-q3.
maya: ops note: because cost savings are material, we should allow Sales/CS opt-in for cost-first customers. otherwise route long-docs to baseline by default.
jordan: add a distribution-shift metric: JS divergence on score histogram >0.08 AND MRR drop >1% should force stricter review.
evan: actioning: i'll add entropy and JS divergence to canary triggers, and implement the slice-aware thresholds. deploying a config patch to staging canary.
sam: i'll run the targeted A/B with routing for long-doc at 10% for 48h and produce per-slice analysis every 6h.
maya: i'll assemble long-doc edge-case prompts and label expected reranking behavior; jordan can help craft cases where nuance matters.
deploy-bot: Scheduling: canary-config v3 (rerank-q3-slice-aware) will deploy to staging canary at 2026-03-21T14:20Z. :gear:
reliability-bot: Created alert `rerank_q3_longdoc_mrr_drop` 1: fires if relative long-doc MRR drop >1.5% for two consecutive 1h windows.
maya: landing plan: if targeted A/B shows persistent >1.5% MRR regression on long-doc but overall cost wins, we gate via routing (long-doc -> baseline) and optionally offer q3 to cost-optimized customers. if stable within thresholds, promote after 72h. will reconvene after first 24h of A/B. :eyes:
